page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-128 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.6 GHz. It features 128 vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 512 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core performance, with the instance placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, achieving 309.76 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 135.09 GB/sec for write operations. Cryptographic capabilities are robust, with the Passmark CPU encryption test reaching top-tier performance in the top 10% due to hardware-accelerated instruction sets like AES and SHA_NI. Ray tracing performance also ranks in the top 10%.

This instance is suited for compute-heavy parallel workloads, database operations, and software compilation, as evidenced by its strong performance in Passmark database tests and Clang compilation benchmarks. While it handles prompt processing for small and medium language models efficiently, text generation for large 70B models is a bottleneck, falling into the bottom 25% of benchmarks. This highlights a tradeoff where the system excels at high-throughput parallel processing but is constrained by the lack of GPU acceleration for heavy generative AI workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-128 is an x86_64 general-purpose instance configured with 128 vCPUs, 64 physical Intel Xeon cores, and 512 GB of RAM. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, this instance relies on its dedicated CPU allocation and high memory bandwidth, which reaches 309.76 GB/sec for large-block reads. Benchmark data shows strong multi-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests, alongside top-tier cryptographic execution. It is highly capable for database operations, software compilation, and static web serving. However, the absence of a GPU limits its efficiency for large-scale LLM text generation, where it performs in the bottom 25%. This makes the instance best suited for enterprise-grade databases, parallel computing, and high-throughput web serving.
